units.translation: But Justice of kindred blood strongly urges him to ward off the hostile spear from his mother who bore him.
the justice of kinship sends him into battle
where Heimsoethius rightly reads προστέρνων στολμῶν [chest-coverings], deleting the gloss πέπλων [robes].
μέγαν προσ-θεῖσαν Αίγίσθῳ [having added a great ... to Aegisthus]
robbing the gods of their honors, he bestows them upon mortals
What other faction then shall I add to this one?
a cutting, having added a lock of hair
and I will add this vote for Orestes
lest he add some evil to evils
having added a great ... to Aegisthus
Hesychius says that the mouth of a river is called προστόμιον [mouth] only in Aeschylus (s.v. προχοή [outpouring]).
from the fine-sanded mouths of the Nile

and I commanded them to supplicate these houses
Another example of this verb was noted by Hasius from Teletes in Stobaeus, Flor. 97, 31: ἄλλον προστρέφειν [to rear another].
some priest of ruin was reared in the house
Another example of this verb was noted by Hasius from Teletes in Stobaeus, Flor. 97, 31: ἄλλον προστρέφειν [to rear another].
with a foolish tongue he brings punishment upon himself
already blunted and rubbed against other houses
that which is rubbed against; pollution

κακόν τι προστριβέν αὐτῇ [some evil rubbed against her], explains Triclinius. It signifies contagion, as Waelius notes, comparing Antiphon p. 127, 2: ὑμῖν τὸ μήνιμα τῶν ἀλιτηρίων προστρίψομαι [I will rub off upon you the wrath of the sinners].
placing upon the city an unbearable pollution
some evil rubbed against her, explains Triclinius. It signifies contagion, as Waelius notes, comparing Antiphon p. 127, 2: I will rub off upon you the wrath of the sinners.
Poetic form for ποτιτρόπαιος [suppliant], see β.
Δέχου δὲ πρευμενῶς ἀλάστορα, οὐ [Receive graciously the avenger, not]
where Orestes confesses himself guilty of murder, but denies that he is still προστρόπαιον [a suppliant], i.e. polluted by the stain.
having come as a suppliant to the hearth
I see a man at the navel-stone, holding a seat abhorred by the gods, a suppliant
for terrible among mortals and gods is the wrath of the suppliant
Poetic form for ποτιτρόπαιος [suppliant], see β.
where it signifies a gathering of suppliant women.
so that I may clearly learn what this gathering of women is
since you are present as escorts of this supplication for me
with the first-murder supplications of Ixion
Thus Auratus for κοπείσης [cut]. It can be preserved if δέρης [of the neck] is written for θερμῷ [warm] with Waelius.
